Name: Atoer
Notes: Described as a burly, capable, tall man; performed comedy sketches on deck in the evenings

Name: Bandong
Notes: Husband of the baboe; joined shore excursions; collected a bees' nest among other things

Name: Gepeng
Notes: Left the ship at Djangkar on 10 March 1899

Name: Radi
Notes: Injured on board while freeing the pennant; broke five ribs, later recovered

Name: the baboe (nursemaid/servant)
Notes: NAME NOT RECORDED. Wife of Bandong; had a son in Buitenzorg

Name: the mandoer (foreman)
Notes: Identical to Atoer; referred to by role more often than by name

Name: the mestri (ship's carpenter)
Notes: NAME NOT RECORDED

Name: Crew (collective)
Notes: De Gids p.519: 52 hands, 'all but four consisting exclusively of natives'

Name: Javanese sailors / stokers
Notes: 48 individuals; never named individually apart from those listed above

Name: Anna Weber-van Bosse
Notes: Author of 'Een jaar aan boord H.M. Siboga'; the only source naming indigenous crew

Name: H.F. Nierstrasz
Notes: Responsible for photography on board

Name: J.H. Huysmans
Notes: In De Gids only anonymous, as 'a skilled draughtsman' (p.519) and 'the draughtsman' (p.536)

Name: Max Weber
Notes: Author of 'Introduction et description' and of the De Gids article

Name: Conrad / Conrat
Notes: Assistant to Klazinga; stayed behind at Surabaya (Anna p.217)

Name: G.F. Tydeman
Notes: Published the hydrographic volume of the Siboga series

Name: Loyer
Notes: Known for his catchphrase 'Poeter Loye' and the stokers' congratulatory card

Name: Noest
Notes: Assistant to Klazinga; musical

Name: Razzio
Notes: 'The stout petty officer'; incident involving the baboe (Anna p.166)

Name: the ship's doctor
Notes: NAME NOT RECORDED in any of the three publications

Name: the steward
Notes: Possibly identical to Nieuwenhuyzen (corporal steward)
